title: Aziridination-Based Crosslinking Enables Site-Resolved Elucidation of Lipid Binding and Protein Conformational Changes.
authors: Tsai, Chia-Lung; Tasnim, Atiya Tahira; Xi, Zhenyu; Kuo, Syuan-Ting; Ramidi, Gopal Reddy; Feng, Jiaxin; Eastabrook, Michael Ryan; Russell, David H; Sui, Xuewu; Yan, Xin
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
one_liner_zh: 该文开发了基于氮丙啶交联的质谱方法（Azi-LPXL-MS）来解析脂质-蛋白结合位点及结合诱导的构象变化，虽以实验方法为主，但结合分子对接和构象分析，对蛋白质结构计算研究有参考价值。
abstract: Lipid-protein interactions play critical roles in cellular function, yet their site-resolved characterization remains challenging due to the dynamic nature of lipid binding and the limited availability of chemoselective strategies for covalently capturing native lipid-protein contacts. Here, we introduce aziridination-based lipid-protein crosslinking coupled with mass spectrometry (Azi-LPXL-MS), a chemoselective strategy that installs an N-H aziridine moiety onto acyl chains of native unsaturated lipids and enables subsequent crosslinking to proximal lysine residues using the amine-reactive reagent disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS). This integrated workflow simultaneously identifies lipid-binding sites and intraprotein peptide-peptide distance constraints, providing direct insight into lipid binding and binding-induced conformational changes within a single experiment. Application of Azi-LPXL-MS to beta-lactoglobulin (BLG) demonstrates these capabilities, consistent with known structural models, while additionally providing solution-phase and conformational information not accessible from static structures alone. The power of the method is further demonstrated in the integral membrane enzyme diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (DGAT1). Azi-LPXL-MS reveals phosphatidic acid (PA)-binding sites and maps lipid-dependent conformational rearrangements across both resolved and previously uncharacterized regions. These data further define an allosteric conformational network linking lipid engagement to distal structural changes. Integrated with site-directed mutagenesis and molecular docking, two potential PA-binding sites in DGAT1, located in a surface pocket and an internal chamber, were identified and functionally validated, further supporting the experimental findings. These results establish Azi-LPXL-MS as a site-resolved method for studying lipid-protein interactions, providing insight into how individual lipid species engage proteins and influence their conformations in biological systems.
abstract_zh: 脂质-蛋白质相互作用在细胞功能中扮演关键角色，然而由于其位点分辨的表征仍具挑战性，这源于脂质结合的动态性质以及用于共价捕获天然脂质-蛋白质接触的化学选择性策略有限。在此，我们引入了基于氮丙啶化的脂质-蛋白质交联结合质谱法（Azi-LPXL-MS），这是一种化学选择性策略，将N-H氮丙啶部分安装到天然不饱和脂质的酰基链上，并通过胺反应性试剂二琥珀酰亚胺辛二酸酯（DSS）实现与邻近赖氨酸残基的交联。这一集成工作流程同时识别脂质结合位点和蛋白质内肽-肽距离约束，在单次实验中直接提供对脂质结合及结合诱导构象变化的洞察。将Azi-LPXL-MS应用于β-乳球蛋白（BLG）展示了这些能力，与已知结构模型一致，同时额外提供了静态结构无法获得的溶液相和构象信息。该方法的威力进一步在整合膜酶二酰甘油酰基转移酶1（DGAT1）中得到展示。Azi-LPXL-MS揭示了磷脂酸（PA）结合位点，并绘制了跨已解析及先前未表征区域的脂质依赖性构象重排。这些数据进一步定义了一个变构构象网络，将脂质参与与远端结构变化联系起来。结合定点突变和分子对接，DGAT1中两个潜在的PA结合位点（位于表面口袋和内部腔室）被识别并功能验证，进一步支持了实验发现。这些结果确立了Azi-LPXL-MS作为研究脂质-蛋白质相互作用的位点分辨方法，为理解个体脂质种类如何参与蛋白质并影响其在生物系统中的构象提供了洞察。
